pages.text: A drug enters the $(l)blood$() and is cleared gradually — that is what sets its strength and duration.
- A pen (into the muscle) and pills — absorbed in 1–2 min.$(br)- A syringe into a vein — immediately.$(br)- A drip — while it drips.
Strength depends on the amount in the blood: about one dose — normal effect, more — stronger, but past a threshold — $(l)overdose$(). Two doses in a row or a dose on top of a drip easily cause it.

$(l)Weight$() matters: a dose is meant for $(cfg)70$() kg — too little for a heavy person, too much for a light one.$(br2)$(l)1 ml = 1 standard dose.$() The label shows the concentration (mg/ml).$(br2)Opioids, alcohol and nicotine build $(l)tolerance$() — they work weaker and shorter.
